Run logs `runs/dev-gold-qwen3-8b`, references `data/eval/gold/dev`.

Both figures are computed over **generated edges that match a reference edge on source and destination**. Direction accuracy asks how often the sign is right on the pairs the model did find, which reference-edge recall cannot say because it requires direction to match before counting an edge at all. Strength macro-F1 is symmetric, unlike strength inflation, so it counts under-statement as well as over-statement.

## How to read this

These are diagnostics, as the proposal labels them, over four development queries. A macro-F1 computed from a handful of edges per class is not a model comparison and carries no interval here.

A class absent from both the references and the predictions is dropped rather than scored zero. Averaging in a class nobody could have got wrong drags the mean toward whichever labels happen to be missing from a small sample, which would make the figure move for reasons that have nothing to do with the model.

A condition with 0 matched edges is shown with `n/a`, not omitted. A row that disappears reads as a condition that was never run; a row of zeros reads as a condition that produced nothing matching the references, which is a finding about that condition.

Graphs are skipped, with a count, when the query has no reference or when the generated graph's cutoff differs from the reference's. The second is not pedantry: the reference was adjudicated under its own as-of discipline, so matching across cutoffs scores edges against evidence that was not yet visible, or withholds evidence that was.

Direction accuracy near 1.000 with low reference-edge recall means the model finds few of the reference pairs but gets the sign right on those it finds. Those are separate failures and the challenge set shows why the distinction matters: reversing an edge leaves every deterministic rule passing, so nothing upstream of a reader catches it.
